section: PROTOCOL §1.1 (targets), §4.1, §4.7 (frozen ladder, added to main 2026-09-1x by PRs #13–#15), §12 (nothing from memory) / SPEC §3.1
severity: **phase 2: thirteen new targets registered and launched under the reviewed discrete method (`run-discrete`, thresholds_v8); the PROTOCOL §4.7 ladder and §4.1 controller/real-space/reciprocal/validator agent structure are NOT what the driver implements — disclosed, not adopted**
description: Targets (operator's list, 2026-09-16): 9ARN 4QO4 8IS2 6CDX 1LZ9 9D5Y 1N7E 1V2X 1L6X 7DVR 6UDY 3DUT 9D5U. Every `targets/targets.yaml` value is the literal output of `https://data.rcsb.org/rest/v1/core/entry/<ID>` executed 2026-09-16 (saved with the run): all X-ray, 1.00–1.70 Å, structure factors released (`status_code_sf` REL); depositor R-work/R-free from `refine[0]`; free-set sizes 528 (4QO4, PROTOCOL §3.7 small-set note; header carries no cross-validation method) to 3587 (3DUT); 9D5Y/9D5U carry a 2 % free set; deposited refinement programs PHENIX (4), REFMAC (4), CNS (4), X-PLOR (1) — the CNS/X-PLOR entries' flag conventions are decided by `autoref/flags.py` from `_refln.status` / `pdbx_r_free_flag` at prep, and a file with no flag column halts that target (PROTOCOL §3.1) rather than generating one. Method: `scripts/onboard_target.sh` (fetch → prep → dossier → verify → noise-floor n=10 → baseline) then `scripts/run_dpdb.sh <T> --max-cycles 8` (correction, solvent, protein_altloc, adp_model ladder of SPEC_DPDB_RUNS §3; paired null control; site-restricted reciprocal step; R-gap, divergence and Metropolis rules of v8), orchestrated by `scripts/run_phase2.sh` (13 in parallel, `AUTOREF_NPROC` 24). No per-target `--refine-extra`: the standing 3QUE/3TC7 overrides are target-specific findings (D421, D496). Hydrogens: the deposited models are refined as deposited (mostly without riding H); PROTOCOL §4.1 as amended on main now permits riding H below 2.0 Å for all thirteen, and 3TC7's −0.011 credit (D488) says it can matter — H is a per-target paired experiment after the base runs (E028 pattern), not part of onboarding, because the ADP-weight optimiser's behaviour on H-bearing models needed a per-target fix (D491, D496). Disclosure: main's PROTOCOL §4.7 (L1–L10 with qFit at L3/L4, a standing `phenix.refine` block with `ordered_solvent=True` every macro-cycle and variants A/B, `solvent_model_select`, `zone_shift`, `backbone_split`) and §4.1 (four cooperating agents) describe a method the harness does not implement; the phase-2 runs follow SPEC_DPDB_RUNS as reviewed on 2026-09-08 (D480/D481). Whether to build the ladder is an operator decision; this row records that the two documents now disagree and which one the runs followed.

severity: **data decision: a structure-factor file with several `_refln` blocks is read from the one block that carries the deposited free set; none or several such blocks still refuse**
description: `autoref/flags.py::read_sf_cif` refused any file with more than one `_refln` block ("multi-block SF files need an explicit decision"). Two phase-2 files are multi-block (local inventory of the RCSB downloads, 2026-09-17): `3DUT-sf.cif` — block `r3dutsf` 74 283 rows, F_meas_au, status o 68 393 / f 3 587 / x 2 303; block `r3dutAsf` 89 104 rows, intensity_meas, status all 'o' (no free set). `7DVR-sf.cif` — block `r7dvrsf` 18 619 rows, F_meas_au + intensity_meas + I+/I−, status o 17 175 / f 882 / x 562, plus a 20-bin `pdbx_r_free_flag`; blocks `r7dvrAsf`/`r7dvrBsf`/`r7dvrCsf` (4 188 / 3 782 / 3 841 rows) are anomalous I+/I− sets with status all 'o'. The other eleven files are single-block (all carry `status` with an 'f' set; 9D5U/9D5Y intensities only, 2 % free; 1N7E carries '<' and 'h' status rows, treated as unmeasured; 6UDY/7DVR/8IS2/9ARN also carry a 20-bin `pdbx_r_free_flag`, cross-checked against status as before). section: PROTOCOL §3.1, §3.3, §3.4 (inherited flags; test set never changes size; data selection) / SPEC §5.1 (prep)
severity: **data rules added to prep, and two phase-2 targets re-prepared before any refinement was judged on them: (a) an amplitude of exactly 0 with a non-zero sigma is not an observation and is dropped like a missing value, counted as `n_dropped_zero_amplitude`; (b) when a file carries both intensities and amplitudes with different coverage and exactly one array covers the number of observations the deposited header reports, that array is the one the depositor refined against and is inherited**
description: Two of the thirteen phase-2 targets halted at gate G3 (`FlagIntegrityError`, the guards working as written), the other eleven passed. **1L6X** (`n_free=3500 from fmodel but 3502 in the frozen prep record`): 19 rows of `F_meas_au` are exactly 0.000 with sigma > 0 (e.g. 26 40 3: F 0.000 σ 271.353; 5 5 46: F 0.000 σ 122.893), two of them flagged 'f'; cctbx/phenix drop F_obs = 0 before refinement (`n_refl.: 35198` of 35 217 in the zero-cycle log), so the frozen test set counted two reflections no refinement can see. `is_placeholder` only caught value = sigma = 0 (D009). Rule (a) reproduces phenix's own exclusion; a zero intensity with non-zero sigma is a genuine weak measurement and is untouched. **9ARN** (`n_free=771 is 137 short of the frozen n_free=908`): the file carries `intensity_meas` for 18 490 measured rows and `F_meas_au` for 15 576 = the header's `n_obs`; the 908 flagged rows all have intensities but only 771 = the header's `n_free` have amplitudes. `choose_data_array` preferred the fuller intensity array (the D009 rule, sound when one array is a placeholder), which enlarged the data selection by 2 914 reflections and the test set by 137 relative to the deposited refinement — R-free on that selection is not commensurable with the header (PROTOCOL §3.4), and phenix's I→F conversion then dropped the 137 (n_refl 15 576). Rule (b): with `targets.yaml header.n_obs` available (the RCSB lookup), the array matching it is inherited; ties or no match fall back to the D009 preference. Both rules are recorded per target in prep.json (`data_choice.reason`, `header_n_obs`, `coverage.*.n_zero_value`, `coverage.*.n_free_usable`). Re-preparation: `autoref prep --target 9ARN --force` and `--target 1L6X --force` (new `--force` flag) replaced the frozen files written at 2026-09-17T04:24Z; nothing had been refined against them except the G3 zero-cycle that raised, and their `rfree_split` JSONs and `checks` rows are superseded. Superseded prep sha256s — 9ARN data.mtz ebc3796b…76b9, flags.mtz 6deaffd2…8e17 (IMEAN/SIGIMEAN, n_free 908); 1L6X data.mtz 3671ce1f…2d4e, flags.mtz 2ad7add4…3fd7 (n_free 3502). The other eleven targets' prep records are unaffected: none has F = 0 rows in the chosen array (their n_dropped counts are on record) and none has two arrays with different coverage except 4QO4/6UDY/7DVR, whose arrays cover the same rows. Tests: `tests/test_flags.py::test_zero_amplitude_rows_are_not_observations`, `::test_header_n_obs_picks_the_array_the_depositor_refined_against`.

section: CLAUDE.md (edit local, run remote) / SPEC_DPDB_RUNS §6 (running it on the pod)
severity: **operating error, no data lost: `scripts/onboard_target.sh` was edited (the exit-code report, PR #18) while eleven instances of it were running on the pod; bash reads a script incrementally, so each instance failed as soon as its noise-floor stage returned (6CDX 05:01Z, 4QO4 05:05Z, 7DVR 05:10Z, the rest as their floors finish), before `baseline` and before its run was launched**
description: Symptom: STATUS ends at `noise_floor ok`, no `baseline start`, no baseline.log; `phase2.log` says `onboarding FAILED — no run launched`. The live sync pushes every local save to `/home/dev/workspace` at once, so a local edit is an edit of the running file. Nothing scientific is affected: the `noise_floor` rows were written before the failure (6CDX σ_select 0.000548, σ_report 0.000634, n 10), every onboarding stage is idempotent (fetch reuses, prep verifies checksums, noise floor resumes finished seeds) and no refinement had been judged. Recovery: `run_phase2.sh --targets "6CDX 4QO4 7DVR"` relaunched at 05:13Z; a one-off reaper (`/home/dev/runs/phase2_reaper.sh`, logged in `phase2_reaper.log`) relaunches each of 8IS2 1LZ9 9D5Y 1N7E 1V2X 6UDY 3DUT 9D5U once its STATUS reads `noise_floor ok` and its original process is gone; 9ARN and 1L6X (relaunched 04:33Z, after the edit) are unaffected. Rule added to CLAUDE.md: never edit a shell script that is running on the pod — the sync makes the edit live; launchers should copy the scripts they run to a per-launch snapshot (to be added to `run_phase2.sh` once its current instances have exited, since that file is running too).

severity: **finding, no rule changed: for the legacy (CNS/REFMAC/X-PLOR-era) phase-2 targets the standard noise floor — ten seeds of one 5-macro-cycle re-refinement of the deposited model — measures convergence variance, not test-set noise, and its credit bar is unreachable; recommendation: a versioned convergence step before the floor, then repeat the legacy runs**
description: Evidence (E034/E034b on 1LZ9, `runs/1LZ9/experiments/e034*_nf_converged/result.json`, ten seeds each, thresholds_v8, no `noise_floor` row written): standing floor σ_select 0.005895 (bar −0.0118), σ_full 0.005568, mean select 0.2872; from the run's one-pass baseline σ_select 0.004219, σ_report 0.006099, mean 0.2828; from the run's six-pass final base σ_select **0.001665**, σ_full 0.001332, mean 0.2774 — 3.5× smaller, with σ_gap unchanged (0.0018 → 0.0020). The model itself moved 0.2941 → 0.2789 → 0.2739 on select over its first passes. Consequences for the phase-2 verdicts: 1LZ9 (σ 0.0059), 6UDY (0.0087), 1L6X (0.0055) and 1V2X (0.0008 but −0.12 on its annealing arm) ended with nothing or little credited because no local change can clear a bar set by convergence spread; 6UDY's −0.019 select gains only cleared a −0.017 bar because its whole model was still settling (its first such cycle was refused by the R-gap gate at +3.0σ_gap, D495, the second credited). A second class of wide bars is genuine: small free sets (9ARN 771 → σ_select 0.0054 against an analytic 0.011; 4QO4 528 → 0.0019; 7DVR 882 → 0.0010). Not changed here: the standing rows, thresholds, or any verdict — a floor is a measurement of the judging protocol's input (D491), and changing that input for a target is a D-row decision the operator should own for thirteen targets at once. Recommendation: `thresholds_v9` with `noise_floor.converge_passes` (or `refine.baseline_macro_cycles`, cf. E030's 15) applied to the baseline before the floor is measured; re-measure the floor from that model for every phase-2 target (`autoref noise-floor --model … --label converged`, which replaces the judging row, D488); repeat the legacy runs from their standing records; quote every phase-2 gain against the mean of that floor, not against the single baseline re-refinement (1LZ9's baseline record sits 0.014 above its own second pass).

section: PROTOCOL §4.3, §4.4 (rewritten on main 2026-09-17 by PRs #22–#24), §6 negative controls, §7 per-change record / SPEC §7–§8
severity: **disclosure: PROTOCOL now defines acceptance against a per-target, per-change-class sham null (≥ 50 unsupported changes through the identical restricted paired protocol; frozen 99th-percentile threshold; Benjamini–Hochberg at FDR 0.05; σ_abs explicitly not an acceptance criterion; weights frozen in restricted comparisons; per-change rows carry null ids, p and q values). The harness (thresholds_v1–v8) and every phase-2 verdict judge on k·σ_abs. Not implemented; nothing killed; disclosed and costed**
description: Timeline: the thirteen phase-2 runs launched 2026-09-17T04:24Z (D501) under the §4.4 then on main (ten-seed σ, k = 2); PRs #22 (`saw/protocol_edits-1`), #23 (`saw/protocol_edits-2`, 'Enhance noise and acceptance criteria', 'Update acceptance criteria and refinement steps') and #24 merged 09:40–09:54Z, when five runs had finished and eight were in flight. Under the new §4.4(a), 'any accept/reject comparison made against σ_abs is a defect'; under §4.4(b) the bar per class is the 99th percentile of ΔR-free-select over ≥ 50 sham instances (waters at random positions without an mFo−DFc peak, altlocs at residues without a Ringer secondary peak, flips at residues without residual, zone shifts into flat density), re-measured at L2, after L4, after the first solvent rebuild and after any adopted parameterisation change. What stands: every phase-2 paired cycle's attributable ΔR-free-select, arms, and per-change rows are on record and can be re-judged against a sham null once measured — the D442 procedure — so the runs were not killed; their credits and promotions (4QO4 ×3, 1N7E, 6CDX, 6UDY so far) are valid under the §4.4 they were judged by and are labelled 'k·σ_abs (pre-D507)' until re-judged. What is missing in the harness: a sham-change generator per change class (`stages/negative_controls.py` runs a single water/altloc control, not ≥ 50 per class); a restricted-paired null measurement stage with frozen weights (the D480 step already runs restricted pairs at standing weights — `optimize_weights: false` — so the machinery exists); per-class quantile thresholds in a versioned file; BH across a target's decisions; the extended per-change row. Cost estimate: 50 shams × 2 arms × ~5 min restricted refinement ≈ 8 CPU-h per class per target; 13 targets × 3 classes ≈ 300 CPU-h ≈ 15 h wall at 20 concurrent on this pod, before any re-judgement. Relation to D506: both findings say the seed σ is the wrong acceptance bar; §4.4(b) measures how much R-free is purchasable by unsupported parameters, D506 measures convergence spread — a converged baseline is still needed before the sham null is meaningful (the null does not transfer across parameter counts, §4.4). Decision for the operator: implement §4.4(b) as thresholds_v9 + new stage and re-judge phase 2, or record phase 2 as a k·σ_abs campaign. Until then CLAUDE.md marks the acceptance rule it describes as the pre-D507 one.

severity: **promotion rule completed: a credited best base that beats the standing record on R-free-select but is worse on R-free-report by more than k·σ_report (k = the v7 divergence multiple, 2.0) does not replace it; `PROMOTE-REPORT-<T>-c<N>` row**
description: Found on 6UDY (independent scorer, `runs/verify_20260917/6UDY_*.json`): the run's c002 credit (attributable −0.0197 on select against a null arm that had drifted to 0.2606 from a 0.2414 baseline — the D506 convergence effect on a CNS-era model, σ_select 0.0087) was promoted under D499 because select improved 0.2414 → 0.2397 against the standing baseline record, while the held-back half went 0.2519 → 0.2555 and the full set 0.2468 → 0.2479. The paired divergence gate (D497) compares the two arms of one cycle and saw none; the promotion comparison compared records on the consulted half only — the selection-bias trap PROTOCOL §3.6 names and D484 was written against. Rule: `_promote_report_check` (run_discrete.py) refuses when report_new − report_standing > k·σ_report; not configured before thresholds_v7, not judged without σ_report. On 6UDY the excess (+0.0036) is within its 2σ_report (σ_report 0.0087 → bound 0.017), so the record stands under the rule as written and is labelled in the results as a within-noise change on the full and report sets; the rule would refuse the same pattern on a target with a floor of ordinary size. Scope: drivers already running keep the code they loaded; the rule applies from the next launch. Test: `tests/test_run_discrete.py::test_promotion_refused_when_report_half_is_worse_than_the_standing_record`.
